The master ingots were prepared using a vacuum arc-melting furnace with raw materials with a 99.99 % purity.
The prepared ingots were ground to remove surface impurities and subjected to hot forging at 1200 ◦C, resulting in bar-shaped specimens with final dimensions of 1.2 × 1.2 mm.
Subsequently, solution treatment was performed by holding the alloy at 1200 ◦C for 2 h, yielding a supersaturated solid solution microstructure.
Following solution treatment, cold rolling was applied with a 20 % rolling reduction — a value determined to balance work hardening and crack prevention.
Finally, the alloy underwent aging treatment at 800 ◦C for 3 h to achieve the desired final microstructure
